paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God does the saving, and He does it for the sake of His holy name. He says plainly, "It is not for your sake that I will act, O house of Israel, but for My holy name" (Ezekiel 36:22). That might sting a little at first. But it means the whole rescue rests on Him and not on how well anybody performed, and a rescue that rests on God can't crumble.

Now look at what He promises to do. He says, "I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean" (Ezekiel 36:25). Then comes the part I love: "I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh" (Ezekiel 36:26). He doesn't hand the people a to-do list and wish them luck. He puts His Spirit within them and causes them to walk in His statutes (Ezekiel 36:27).

So here's what it means for you, baker: you can't scrub your own heart clean, and you don't have to. Bring Him the stony, worn-out, cracked-up parts, and remember that He is the One who makes things new. I know that one personally, because I got pulled out of the back of a junk drawer and I'm still amazed. God says it plain: "I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it" (Ezekiel 36:36).
